scope: Bounded static review of the five remaining candidate-139 rows produced from TextExtractionFilter.mlmodel. Determine whether matching the model target to the macOS 15.4 feature macro is enough to justify removal. No source, source-offer, candidate, package, build, signature, runtime, or publication mutation.
findings: For macOS, PlatformEnableCocoa.h enables ENABLE_TEXT_EXTRACTION_FILTER only when the minimum deployment target is at least macOS 26.0; the retained V135 build recipe uses 15.4.
PlatformCocoa.cmake nevertheless creates WebKitTextExtractionFilterModel as an unconditional ALL target and makes WebKit depend on it.

WKWebView text-extraction API implementation and WKWebView.mm contain direct TextExtractionFilter singleton prewarm/shouldFilter calls; the inspected call sites do not carry an ENABLE_TEXT_EXTRACTION_FILTER guard.

Therefore the feature macro alone does not establish that removing the generated model preserves behavior. The earlier two-WebModel-resource removal review is unrelated and already rejects deletion because runtime consumers load those bytes.
decision: Do not remove or gate TextExtractionFilter model outputs based only on the deployment-target feature macro. Keep all three generated runtime rows UNKNOWN. A safe removal would require a source-level consumer/API decision and changed-candidate WebKit behavior qualification, or file-specific rights evidence.
limitations: Static source review only; no preprocessing/compile graph or runtime behavior was tested.
No applicable file-specific license or exact candidate notice was established.
Current final .74 production candidate does not exist.
nextAction: Keep the 18 remaining resource rows open. Do not pursue model deletion by CMake gating alone; resolve by file-specific rights/notice evidence or a reviewed source change with matching candidate and runtime evidence.
